1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif typeface with adequate line height and spacing, though letter spacing appears default rather than notably generous.

2.why: Instructional text is in sentence case with no italics or dense paragraphs; only the small 'YOUR ONLINE BANK' brand label is set in all-caps.

3.why: Content sits in a narrow single-column card with large text and buttons, a layout that would reflow cleanly to a mobile screen, although the screenshots themselves are desktop-width.

4.why: Every instruction is a single short plain-language sentence, e.g. 'Set up an extra check for protected payments.' and 'Multi-factor authentication is active.'

5.why: No field shows an example or placeholder of the expected format; Email, Mobile number, Identity code and Authenticator code inputs are all empty with no hints.

6.why: No screen contains more than one short line of instructional text, so no long block of reading is required to proceed.

7.why: The manual secret and recovery codes are rendered as ordinary text that could likely be selected and copied, but no explicit copy button or affordance is provided.

8.why: Step 4 offers only a typed 'Manual secret' (lu3909HaurbTsvRHRoKks7ezo1c) with no QR code or any equivalent alternative to manual entry.

9.why: The fields are standard labelled text inputs, but nothing in the screenshots confirms or denies autofill and password manager support.

10.why: Each step has a clear bold heading and one prominent blue primary button, though there is no explicit step counter or progress indicator.

11.why: Every screen presents exactly one main action (Continue, Verify and continue, Create secure setup code, Confirm authenticator, Generate recovery codes, I have stored these codes, Sign out).

12.why: Some outcomes are stated plainly ('Multi-factor authentication is active.'), but transitions such as a code being sent are not announced, and the user is simply shown the next form.

13.why: There are no resend-code, reveal or hide controls; the only recovery affordances are a persistent 'Generate recovery codes' button and a generic 'Please try again' after failure.

14.why: The error 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.' is non-blaming and suggests a fix, but it never states what the actual problem was.

15.why: No countdown, timer or timeout warning appears on any screen, so no visible time pressure is imposed on reading or code entry.
